key_patterns.name: Multiplex social layers with differing intensities
key_patterns.description: Contacts are partitioned into family, work_school, and community layers; family is dense and frequent, work/school moderate, community sparser and intermittent.
key_patterns.relevance: Supports layer-specific interaction frequencies and influence weights; essential for reproducing realistic diffusion pathways.

key_patterns.name: Homophily by age_group and occupation
key_patterns.description: Tie formation is more likely among agents sharing age_group and/or occupation; households are strongly age/role correlated; workplaces/schools cluster by occupation.
key_patterns.relevance: Homophily concentrates norms, creating pockets of rapid adoption and pockets of resistance; informs group-specific thresholds and seeding.

key_patterns.name: Risk-perception heterogeneity
key_patterns.description: Agents have risk_perception in [0,1]; expected to be non-uniform across age_group/occupation (e.g., healthcare/white-collar higher than blue-collar; older age groups higher than youth).
key_patterns.relevance: Risk perception modulates intrinsic adoption propensity and sensitivity to social signals; use as a covariate in adoption rules.

key_patterns.name: Asymmetric adjacency lists possible
key_patterns.description: Edges in social_network.json may not be perfectly symmetric across layers.
key_patterns.relevance: Model must reconcile directed/undirected assumptions; asymmetry impacts exposure counts and influence computation.

key_patterns.name: State persistence
key_patterns.description: Panel structure suggests wearing_mask is temporally autocorrelated (habit formation) and increases after received_info.
key_patterns.relevance: Include retention (stickiness) and dropout probabilities; lagged effects from information reception to behavior.

key_distributions.name: Risk perception distribution
key_distributions.description: Model risk_perception ~ Beta(alpha, beta), potentially stratified by age_group and occupation.
key_distributions.parameters: alpha_hat, beta_hat (overall and optionally group-specific); estimate via MLE from agent_attributes.csv

key_distributions.name: Layer-specific degree distributions
key_distributions.description: Family degrees are low with high clustering; work/school moderate; community heavy-tailed/lognormal.
key_distributions.parameters: For each layer L ∈ {family, work_school, community}: degree mean μ_L, std σ_L; fit Lognormal(μ_L, σ_L) or empirical PMF from social_network.json

key_distributions.name: Adoption hazard distribution (conditional on info and peers)
key_distributions.description: Daily probability of adopting follows a logistic function of covariates (risk_perception, neighbor adoption share, info state).
key_distributions.parameters: Logit coefficients: β0 (baseline), β_risk, β_peer_family, β_peer_work, β_peer_community, β_info, plus lag terms

key_distributions.name: Retention (persistence) and dropout
key_distributions.description: Probability of continuing to wear a mask once adopted vs reverting.
key_distributions.parameters: p_stay (retain), p_drop = 1 - p_stay; optionally functions of info and policy status; estimate from agent_state_panel CSV

key_relationships.relationship: Positive association: receiving pro-mask information increases same-day and next-day adoption likelihood.
key_relationships.strength: To be estimated; expect moderate-to-strong (β_info > 0, statistically significant)

key_relationships.relationship: Higher fraction of masked neighbors (especially family) increases adoption probability.
key_relationships.strength: Strongest for family, moderate for work/school, weakest for community; quantify via β_peer_*

key_relationships.relationship: Higher baseline risk perception increases both initial adoption and ongoing adherence.
key_relationships.strength: Expected moderate; interacts with peer influence (β_risk > 0)

key_relationships.relationship: Students have higher work_school degrees, white-collar more community ties; age affects household composition.
key_relationships.strength: Structural; derive directly from social_network.json and agent_attributes.csv

layer_influence_weights.source: social_network.json structure; calibrated with agent_state_panel transitions
layer_influence_weights.notes: Scales peer adoption shares by layer salience; refine via calibration to maximize likelihood of observed behavior.

activation_schedule.source: Occupational roles in agent_attributes.csv and conventional contact patterns
activation_schedule.notes: Implements day-of-week activation; community activation frequency can be tuned.

edge_directionality.value: Treat as undirected by symmetrizing adjacency lists
edge_directionality.notes: Symmetrize to avoid exposure biases; alternatively retain direction and use in information diffusion only.

baseline_adoption_prob_without_info.source: agent_state_panel CSV pre-info days; intercept β0 in logistic model
baseline_adoption_prob_without_info.notes: Daily probability for low-risk, low-peer-exposure agents; to be calibrated.

risk_sensitivity_beta.source: agent_state_panel CSV regression of wearing_mask on risk_perception
risk_sensitivity_beta.notes: Logit coefficient; higher means stronger effect of risk perception on adoption.

peer_influence_betas_by_layer.source: Combine social_network.json with panel to compute neighbor_mask_share and fit logistic
peer_influence_betas_by_layer.notes: Coefficients on neighbor masked share by layer; expected family > work > community.

retention_probability.notes: Stickiness of adoption; can be group-specific.

dropout_probability.notes: May increase when peers or info decline; calibrate with lag terms.

info_transmission_prob_by_layer.source: Estimate from panel: P(info_t=1 | neighbor_info_{t-1} share) by layer
info_transmission_prob_by_layer.notes: Daily per-contact probability; can be modeled via logistic with per-layer coefficients rather than fixed probs.

info_decay_rate.notes: Approx half-life ~14 days; use exponential forgetting.

external_info_rate.source: Intercept term for info process (mass media/background)
external_info_rate.notes: Daily chance of receiving info without network exposure; calibrate.

group_multipliers_age.notes: Multiplicative factor on adoption odds; to match adoption_inequality_index targets.

group_multipliers_occupation.source: agent_attributes.csv and panel; if Healthcare is present
group_multipliers_occupation.notes: Adjusts both adoption propensity and info receptivity.

mask_requirement_by_layer.source: Scenario input (not in data); 1.0 indicates mandated, 0.0 not
mask_requirement_by_layer.notes: Time-varying schedules should be supported; feeds noncompliance metric.

enforcement_strength.notes: Boosts adoption odds when mandates apply and reduces noncompliance.

noncompliance_noise.notes: Lower bound of noncompliance due to constraints/preferences.

mask_inventory_capacity_per_capita.notes: Average reusable masks per person supported by supply chain.

restock_quantity_per_capita.notes: New masks per person per restock; adjust to control stockout frequency.

mask_usage_rate_per_wearer_per_day.source: Assumption for reusable masks (10-day lifetime equivalent)
mask_usage_rate_per_wearer_per_day.notes: Determines depletion rate and mask_availability metric.

mask_efficacy.source: Literature defaults; refine if empirical data available
mask_efficacy.notes: Estimated_transmission_reduction ≈ 1 - (1 - e_sc * adoption)^2 with mixing approximation; can be refined.

initial_seeding_rule.value: Bernoulli for each agent with p = 0.2 * risk_perception
initial_seeding_rule.notes: Alternative: seed top decile of risk_perception deterministically.

time_horizon_days.notes: Adjust based on desired evaluation window.

adoption_inequality_index_method.value: Between-group variance of adoption rates across age_group and occupation; optional Gini over agent-level adoption probabilities
adoption_inequality_index_method.notes: Compute per-day and over final N days; track trend.

noncompliance_rate_method.value: Share of agents not wearing masks on edges/locations where mask_requirement_by_layer > 0
noncompliance_rate_method.source: Policy schedule + simulated states + layer memberships

mask_availability_method.value: Track retailer inventory state; report fraction of days with stock > 0 and count of stockout days
mask_availability_method.notes: Availability can gate adoption when stock is 0.

estimated_transmission_reduction_method.value: Compute effective contact reduction = sum_over_layers(weight_L * adoption_L * efficacy_effect)
estimated_transmission_reduction_method.source: Mask efficacy, adoption by layer, layer weights
estimated_transmission_reduction_method.notes: Use pair-protection formula: 1 - (1 - e_sc * A - e_wp * A + e_sc * e_wp * A^2) with A=adoption.

preprocessing_steps.step: Validate agent_id integrity and join keys
preprocessing_steps.purpose: Ensure one-to-one mapping across agent_attributes.csv, social_network.json, and state panel.
One-hot encode age_group and occupation; clip risk_perception to [0,1].

preprocessing_steps.step: Build multiplex graphs and symmetrize edges
preprocessing_steps.purpose: Construct per-layer adjacency matrices/lists; enforce undirected assumption or mark direction if retained.

preprocessing_steps.step: Compute per-agent degree and neighbor composition by layer
preprocessing_steps.purpose: Derive exposure features (neighbor adoption share, neighbor info share) for calibration.
Create lag variables: wearing_mask_{t-1}, received_info_{t-1}, neighbor_mask_share_{t-1} by layer.
Hold out last T days (e.g., 20%) or use rolling-origin evaluation to validate out-of-sample.

calibration_strategy.calibration_approach: Use a two-stage likelihood-based approach with hierarchical pooling. Stage 1: Information diffusion. Fit logistic or complementary log-log models for received_info_t ~ intercept + sum_L(w_L * neighbor_info_share_{t-1,L}) + group dummies + random intercepts by occupation/age_group. Extract per-layer info transmission parameters and external_info_rate. Stage 2: Adoption dynamics. Fit a discrete-time hazard/logistic model for wearing_mask_t ~ β0 + β_info * received_info_{t-1} + sum_L(β_peer_L * neighbor_mask_share_{t-1,L}) + β_risk * risk_perception + retention term γ * wearing_mask_{t-1} + policy/enforcement terms + group interactions. Optionally, Bayesian hierarchical modeling for partial pooling across groups. Translate fitted coefficients into simulation parameters (daily probabilities via logistic link). If direct likelihood fitting is insufficient due to unobserved heterogeneity, apply simulation-based calibration (e.g., Approximate Bayesian Computation or likelihood-free inference) targeting the evaluation metrics trajectories.
calibration_strategy.validation_strategy: Out-of-sample time validation: simulate from calibrated parameters over the validation window using the same initial state at split, and compare trajectories for overall_mask_adoption_rate, peak, time_to_target_adoption, and sustained_adoption_rate. Group-level validation: compare adoption by age_group/occupation and compute adoption_inequality_index. Network-stratified checks: compare adoption by degree quantiles and by layer exposure. Posterior predictive checks or parametric bootstrap to assess uncertainty. Sensitivity analysis: perturb key parameters (β_peer_L, β_info, retention, enforcement, supply) ±20% and examine robustness of metrics.

file_summaries:
Semantic metadata summary for agent_attributes.csv

- Overall structure/type:
  - Flat CSV table; one row per agent (no nesting). Primary key: agent_id.

- Columns and meanings:
  - agent_id (int): Unique identifier for each agent; used to join with network/edge lists and state variables.
  - age_group (categorical string): Demographic segment (e.g., Youth, Young Adult, Middle Age); proxy for homophily, contact patterns, and susceptibility to peer norms.
  - occupation (categorical string): Role/context (e.g., Student, Blue Collar, White Collar); determines workplace/school layer membership and associated contact rates.
  - risk_perception (float in [0,1]): Baseline perceived health risk; higher values imply greater intrinsic propensity to wear masks and/or lower thresholds for adoption.

- Relationships/nesting:
  - No nested elements. Each record is independent.
  - agent_id is the join key to external artifacts (e.g., social network edges, households, locations).
  - age_group and occupation define groupings for layered networks (school/work, age cohorts) and for homophilous tie probabilities.

- How to inform simulation:
  - Initialize agents with these attributes.
  - Seed initial mask-wearing: deterministic threshold on risk_perception or Bernoulli with p = risk_perception (optionally stratified by age/occupation).
  - Influence dynamics: weight social influence by risk_perception (more risk-aware agents adopt/retain more easily); allow age/occupation-specific thresholds or conformity parameters.
  - Network construction: create multilayer contacts (e.g., school for Students, workplace for Blue/White Collar); increase within-group tie probability by shared age_group/occupation.
  - Scheduling/contact rates: set frequency/intensity by occupation (e.g., Students higher school contacts) and age_group.
  - Policy targeting: enable group-specific interventions (messages to low-risk-perception groups or by occupation).
  - Data hygiene: ensure uniqueness of agent_id, categorical encoding for age_group/occupation, and risk_perception clipped to [0,1].

Semantic metadata summary for social_network.json:

- Data structure and type:
  - JSON object (dictionary) mapping agent IDs (as strings) to nested objects.
  - Each nested object contains three arrays of integers. This is a multiplex adjacency-list representation (sparse graph), unweighted and categorical by layer.

- Meaning of keys/columns:
  - Top-level keys: stringified agent IDs (e.g., "0", "1"). Convert to integers for internal use.
  - Nested keys:
    - family: IDs of household/family contacts.
    - work_school: IDs of workplace or school contacts.
    - community: IDs of broader community/social contacts.
  - Array values: neighbor agent IDs; assumed to reference the same global agent index set (likely 0–99 based on samples).

- Relationships/nested elements:
  - Each agent has up to three adjacency lists, one per layer; edges are unweighted and layer-specific.
  - Directionality is not explicitly stated; verify symmetry if undirected behavior is desired (some lists may be asymmetric).
  - No timestamps, frequencies, or strengths; no self-loops shown; potential empty arrays should be handled.
  - This forms a three-layer multiplex network sharing the same node set, with disjoint edge types by layer.

- How this informs simulation entities/interactions:
  - Agents: one agent per ID; maintain state variables (e.g., mask_wearing: boolean/probability, susceptibility to influence, thresholds).
  - Networks: build three separate graphs or one graph with edge attribute layer ∈ {family, work_school, community}.
  - Interaction rules: propagate mask-wearing via social influence along edges, with layer-specific influence weights or contact rates (e.g., higher in family, medium in work/school, lower in community).
  - Scheduling: consider different activation patterns per layer (e.g., family daily, work/school weekdays, community sporadic).
  - Initialization and calibration: choose initial adopters; compute per-agent neighborhood composition by layer; handle directed vs. undirected assumptions; deduplicate neighbors; optionally infer degree-based heterogeneity.
  - Metrics: track adoption over time overall and by layer/degree; allow interventions targeted by layer (e.g., workplace campaigns) using these adjacency lists.

- Data structure and type: CSV file with a tabular, time-indexed panel of agent states. Each row is a snapshot of one agent on a given day. Primary key is composite (day, agent_id). No nested elements.
- Columns/keys:
  - day (int): discrete simulation timestep (t ≥ 0).
  - agent_id (int): unique identifier for an agent; reused across days to track trajectories.
  - wearing_mask (bool): agent’s behavioral state at that day (adopted vs. not).
  - received_info (bool): whether the agent has been exposed to pro-mask information by that day.
- Relationships:
  - Panel structure: multiple rows per agent across days; time series suitable for modeling transitions.
  - State dependency: wearing_mask is expected to be influenced by received_info (and possibly prior-day states); received_info likely spreads via network contagion.
  - No explicit network structure included; edges must be sourced or generated elsewhere.
- How it informs the simulation:
  - Initialization: day 0 rows provide initial agent states (e.g., starting with no masks/info as in sample).
  - Agent schema: each agent maintains two state variables per timestep: received_info and wearing_mask.
  - Dynamics calibration: estimate transition probabilities from data, e.g., P(info_t=1 | neighbors’ info), P(mask_t=1 | info_t or info_{t-1}), persistence/decay rates, and baseline adoption without info.
  - Validation/training: compare simulated trajectories to observed panel to fit parameters; log simulation outputs in the same schema for evaluation.
  - Missing components: social network must be defined externally (static or time-varying) to drive received_info transitions; this file does not contain edges or interaction weights.
